findings.evidence: The proof is `h.isNullSet_ne_mfderiv` + `hu.hasWeakMFDerivOnBordered` + `congr_deriv_of_isNullSet`. Each is a direct wrapper of `HasWeakMFDerivOnGroupoid.isNullSet_ne_mfderiv` (l.362), `ContMDiffOn.hasWeakMFDerivOnGroupoid` (l.277, takes `hG`) and `HasWeakMFDerivOnGroupoid.congr_deriv_of_isNullSet` (l.298, takes `hG`).
findings.fix: Add `hasWeakMFDerivOnGroupoid_iff_isNullSet_ne_mfderiv [IsManifold J 1 X] [HasGroupoid X G] [IsManifold I ∞ M] [CompleteSpace F] (hG : G.maximalAtlas X ⊆ IsManifold.maximalAtlas J 1 X) (hu : ContMDiffOn J I n u s) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hs : IsOpen s) : HasWeakMFDerivOnGroupoid G J I u du s ↔ IsNullSet J {x ∈ s | du x ≠ mfderiv J I u x}` in the Groupoid section. Derive the bordered version from it with `borderedHolomorphicGroupoid_maximalAtlas_subset (by simp)`.
findings.issue: `hasWeakMFDerivOnBordered_iff_isNullSet_ne_mfderiv` is proved only for bordered surfaces, though its proof uses only groupoid-level lemmas. Surfaces without boundary get no iff.

findings.evidence: The body `simpa using (hasWeakMFDerivOnGroupoid_univ.2 h).isNullSet_ne_mfderiv hu.contMDiffOn hn isOpen_univ` uses only the groupoid API. A grep for `theorem HasWeakMFDeriv\.` / `HasWeakMFDerivGroupoid.isNullSet` finds no global analogue.
findings.fix: Prove `HasWeakMFDerivGroupoid.isNullSet_ne_mfderiv [IsManifold J 1 X] [HasGroupoid X G] [IsManifold I ∞ M] (h : HasWeakMFDerivGroupoid G J I u du) (hu : ContMDiff J I n u) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : IsNullSet J {x | du x ≠ mfderiv J I u x}` with the same `simpa`. Make the bordered statement a term-mode specialization of it.
findings.issue: `HasWeakMFDerivBordered.isNullSet_ne_mfderiv` routes through `hasWeakMFDerivOnGroupoid_univ` but is stated only for the bordered case. There is no `HasWeakMFDerivGroupoid.isNullSet_ne_mfderiv`.

summary: The two `on s` specializations are at the right level, but the iff and the whole-surface `mfderiv` agreement repeat a generic groupoid argument for the bordered case only. Both should be proved once at the groupoid level, with the bordered lemmas as one-line specializations.
